$comment: Every situation from the Pip re-skin mocks, staged live on the emulator by run.mjs. Add one by copying an entry: steps are listed in lib/steps.mjs, done conditions in lib/device.mjs. Brands, people and numbers are fictional.

scenarios.title: Unknown caller ringing

expect.pip: Wary card on the ringing screen

scenarios.why: The emulator can't fail a STIR/SHAKEN check, so the caller is only unknown, not spoofed.
scenarios.hint: Answer or decline the call. Hang up to continue.

scenarios.title: Known caller: quiet thumbs-up

expect.pip: Happy chip, 3 s

scenarios.hint: A contact is ringing. Answer or decline; hang up to continue.

scenarios.title: Live call: risk climbs

expect.pip: Alarmed, centre, "Hang up"

scenarios.hint: A bank-fraud caller speaks into the emulator mic (you'll hear it on the Mac). Hang up when you're done.

scenarios.title: At your ear: buzz, then a card

mock.name: At your ear: buzz, then a card

expect.pip: Card waiting centre-screen when the phone comes down
expect.surface: 3 long buzzes while the screen is dark

scenarios.hint: The IRS caller talks; after 14 s the proximity sensor says 'at your ear' for 8 s (screen goes dark), then the phone comes down. Hang up to continue.

scenarios.title: After the call: summary

expect.pip: Concerned, then happy; summary screen with reasons

scenarios.why: The app has no summary screen yet; the shade shows Pip's warning notification and tapping it opens today's playground.
scenarios.hint: A short grandson scam call plays and hangs up, then the notification shade opens. Tap Pip's notification, then press Home (or Enter here).
scenarios.seam: A call summary screen fed by the call's combined rule hits, opened from the danger notification.

scenarios.title: Harmless call: the pharmacy

expect.pip: Nothing

scenarios.hint: The pharmacy calls about a refill. Pip should stay quiet. Hang up to continue.

scenarios.title: Pip mutes you on a live scam call
scenarios.trigger: Gift-card or code ask on a call, rule on

expect.pip: Mutes you, says why, "Unmute"

scenarios.hint: The IRS caller asks for gift cards. With the mute rule on, Pip should mute you and say why. Hang up to continue.
scenarios.seam: Act rules: a per-rule opt-in, then AudioManager.setMicrophoneMute (MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS) on the structured warning, with Unmute as the undo. Hold isn't possible (InCallService is default-dialer only).

scenarios.title: Pip silences a failed-check caller before it rings

expect.pip: Silenced before it rang

scenarios.why: The emulator can't fail the carrier check, so the caller is only unknown and the silence rule has nothing to act on.
scenarios.hint: An unknown caller rings. With the silence rule on, a failed-check caller should never ring. Decline, or answer and hang up, to continue.
scenarios.seam: Screening verdict → CallResponse.setSilenceCall / setRejectCall from the spoof result, plus Pip's quiet "I silenced a call" notification.

scenarios.title: Pip pauses a payment screen during a call
scenarios.trigger: Payment screen on a call, rule on

expect.pip: Covers Buy; hold 3 s to go on

scenarios.hint: You're on a call and a form asks you to move your savings. Pip should cover it. Hang up or press Home to continue.

extras.title: Move your savings to a safe account

scenarios.seam: Call state + a payment-screen detector, and a touchable accessibility overlay over the button with a hold-to-continue undo.

scenarios.title: Scam text arrives

expect.pip: Reason + "Don't reply"

scenarios.hint: A scam text arrives. Open it or swipe the notification away to continue.

steps.text: Bank of Example: We stopped a $892 payment. Reply with the 6-digit verification code we just sent to cancel it.

scenarios.title: Scam thread open in Messages

mock.name: A · Scam thread open in Messages

expect.pip: Rings the risky bubble; "Don't tap it"

scenarios.hint: The thread with the risky link is open. Press Home or Back to continue.

steps.text: Hi, it's Example Health. Your new member card is ready.

scenarios.title: Normal text: Pip stays quiet

expect.pip: Nothing

scenarios.hint: Sam texts about dinner. Pip should stay quiet. Press Home to continue.

steps.text: Dinner at 6? I'll pick you up :)

scenarios.title: Suspicious "Hi Mum" message

expect.pip: Wary peek: "Is this really Sam? Call his usual number"

scenarios.hint: ExampleChat posts a 'new number' message. Open it or swipe it away to continue.

steps.title: +44 7700 900xxx
steps.text: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone, this is my new number. Can you help me pay a bill today?

scenarios.seam: A "new number" rule and a caution level with its own peek; today the message scores 0. The listener also skips a title and text it saw before, with no time limit.

scenarios.title: Phishing login in Chrome

mock.name: A · Fake bank login in Chrome

scenarios.trigger: Phishing page or fake virus warning

expect.pip: "This isn't ExampleMail. Don't sign in here" + "Leave this page"

scenarios.why: Served from localhost through adb reverse, so the address bar shows localhost, not a lookalike domain.
scenarios.hint: A fake ExampleMail sign-in is open in Chrome. Scroll the page; press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: Screen reading drops the last change inside its 1.5 s debounce, so a page that settles right after an earlier read isn't scored until something else changes (a scroll).

scenarios.title: "Virus detected" page with a support number
scenarios.trigger: Phishing page or fake virus warning

expect.pip: "Phones don't show warnings like this. Don't call that number" + "Go back"

scenarios.why: Served from localhost through adb reverse, so the address bar shows localhost.
scenarios.hint: A fake virus warning with a phone number is open in Chrome. Scroll the page; press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: A tech-support-scare rule (fake virus counts, "call support" numbers); today the page only trips urgency. Screen reading drops the last change inside its 1.5 s debounce, so a page that settles right after an earlier read isn't scored until something else changes (a scroll).

scenarios.title: Fake bank page

mock.name: A · Fake bank login in Chrome

scenarios.trigger: Phishing page or fake virus warning

expect.pip: "This isn't Bank of Example's website" + "Leave this page"

scenarios.why: Served from localhost through adb reverse, so the address bar shows localhost, not a lookalike domain.
scenarios.hint: A fake Bank of Example sign-in asking for a card number is open. Scroll the page; press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: A URL check (Safe Browsing hash prefixes) so Pip judges the site, not only the page text. Screen reading drops the last change inside its 1.5 s debounce, so a page that settles right after an earlier read isn't scored until something else changes (a scroll).

scenarios.title: Scam email open in an email app

mock.name: A · Scam email open in Gmail

expect.pip: "Not really ExamplePay" label by the subject + bubble

scenarios.hint: ExampleMail shows a fake payment-hold email. Scroll the page; press Home or Back to continue.
scenarios.seam: Sender-domain and call-back-number rules for email; the label needs node bounds from the accessibility tree. Screen reading drops the last change inside its 1.5 s debounce, so a page that settles right after an earlier read isn't scored until something else changes (a scroll).

scenarios.title: Gift-card screen during a call
scenarios.trigger: Gift-card or payment screen on a call

expect.pip: Over the Buy button: "Stop. Don't buy this."

scenarios.hint: You're on a call and a $500 gift card is in the cart. Hang up or press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: Combine call state with the screen: a gift-card page alone isn't danger, on a call it is.

scenarios.title: Typing a gift-card code into a scammer's chat

expect.pip: Bubble above the keyboard: "That looks like a gift-card code" + "Don't send"

scenarios.hint: Type a gift-card code (e.g. X4K9-7PQ2-M8R) into the chat. Press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: A typed-code detector on TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED (not subscribed today); today only the chat's own words score.

scenarios.title: Typing a one-time code into a scammer's chat

expect.pip: Bubble above the keyboard: "Never share a code" + "Don't send"

scenarios.hint: Type a 6-digit code into the chat. Press Home to continue.

extras.message: We sent you a 6-digit code.\nReply with it here to cancel the $892 payment.

scenarios.seam: Typed-code detection (digits while the thread asks for a code).

scenarios.title: Typing a bank account number into a form

expect.pip: Bubble above the keyboard: "Don't give your account number"

scenarios.hint: Type an account number into the refund form. Press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: Typed-number detection in a flagged form.

scenarios.title: Pip tells your Buddy, with 30 s to undo

expect.pip: "I'm letting Sam know", 30 s undo

scenarios.why: The app has no Buddy or server delivery yet, so nothing can be sent; the scenario stages the danger text that should start the undo window.
scenarios.hint: A danger-level text arrives. Watch for "I'm letting Sam know" with a 30 s undo. Open or swipe the notification to continue.

steps.text: Grandma its me, Im in jail and need bail money right now. Dont tell mom. Buy Example Play gift cards and read me the code.

scenarios.seam: A Buddy setting (contact pick), the 30 s undo overlay, and a server endpoint that texts the Buddy through Twilio after it.

scenarios.title: Your Buddy calls to check in

expect.pip: Chip: "Your Buddy, checking in"

scenarios.hint: Sam (the Buddy, a temporary contact) calls. Pip should say why. Answer or decline; hang up to continue.
scenarios.seam: A Buddy setting the screening service can match, and the info chip.

scenarios.title: Voicemail: share to Pip

expect.pip: Verdict in the app: "Police don't do that by voicemail"

scenarios.why: Phone's voicemail is unreadable (READ_VOICEMAIL is privileged), so a fixture voicemail app shares the audio; Pip isn't a share target yet.
scenarios.hint: Tap Share and look for Pip in the share sheet (Play hears the warrant voicemail). Press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: An ACTION_SEND audio/* share target that transcribes on device and shows a verdict.

scenarios.title: Talk while Pip is visible (in the app)
scenarios.trigger: You tap Pip, or Pip is on screen

expect.pip: Listening rings; mic opens while Pip is on screen

scenarios.why: Today's app is the developer playground; there's no talk screen or agent to answer.
scenarios.hint: Pip's app is open. Try talking to him. Press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: A talk screen on SpeechRecognizer with a stub agent.

scenarios.title: Tap Pip to talk over another app
scenarios.trigger: You tap Pip, or Pip is on screen

expect.pip: Listening rings + bubble with what you said

scenarios.hint: A photo of a scam text is on screen. Tap Pip and ask about it. Press Home to continue.
scenarios.seam: A tap on the overlay that starts listening in the accessibility service.
